path_decisions.rationale: profit_target_exit uses single effective_pct for ALL entries in the series (not per-entry); trailing_stop is the complementary exit that compounds this flaw by also lacking per-entry granularity

Trailing stop computes close < highest - ATR*mult but BacktestEngine enters at next-bar open after signal while trailing uses close-to-close; this timing mismatch creates phantom exit triggers in backtest

BacktestEngine ignores exit signals while not in position but strategy exits can overlap re-entry on same bar; min_conditions affects which bars have overlapping entry+exit causing trade count distortion

min_conditions counts vol_ok toward entry threshold but entry signal strength is hardcoded (not computed from conditions_met/total_conditions); this disconnect means Kelly sizing operates on wrong conviction level

evidence: quantflow/strategy/templates/_runtime.py:131-173 -- profit_target_exit() takes a single profit_take_pct float, applies identical effective_pct to ALL entries regardless of entry RSI or direction

quantflow/strategy/templates/trend_following.py:257-268 -- RSI-adaptive computes avg_entry_rsi = float(rsi[entries].mean()), a single global mean applied to ALL trades; with 100+ entries this converges to ~50 making adaptation dead code

quantflow/strategy/templates/trend_following.py:283-292 -- trailing stop loop tracks highest since entry using close prices; BacktestEngine enters at next-bar open (line 114: entry_price = close_values[i] * (1 + fee)) while trailing stop exit compares to current close, creating bar-boundary timing inconsistency

quantflow/strategy/research/backtest.py:110-121 -- entry/exit loop uses prev_idx (i-1) signals to trade at bar i open; but strategy trailing stops and profit targets use same-bar close comparison, so exit signal at bar N fires trade at bar N+1 open, potentially missing the optimal exit by 1 bar

quantflow/strategy/templates/trend_following.py:164-171 -- entry counts vol_ok as 1 of 4 conditions toward min_conditions=4; but strength=0.8 is hardcoded regardless of whether 3/4 or 4/4 conditions passed, disconnecting signal conviction from Kelly sizing

quantflow/strategy/templates/mean_reversion.py:36 -- volume_threshold default=0.8 in code vs 1.2 in YAML; code default dominates making vol_ok nearly free condition, inflating entries with weak volume confirmation

quantflow/strategy/templates/volatility_breakout.py:205-213 -- long_count and short_count share atr_spike, bb_expanding, vol_surge, previous_squeeze as common conditions; direction is determined ONLY by close > bb_upper vs close < bb_lower, making 4 of 5 conditions direction-agnostic

quantflow/strategy/templates/mean_reversion.py:138 -- entries = (long_count >= self._min_conditions) | (short_count >= self._min_conditions) merges long+short into single boolean series; profit_target_exit then has no way to distinguish direction

quantflow/signal/risk_engine.py:105-108 -- _check_strategy_budget iterates ALL portfolio.positions.values() without filtering by signal.strategy_id, summing total exposure not per-strategy exposure; budget limit is per-strategy but check sums cross-strategy

quantflow/strategy/validation/signal_quality.py:26-28 -- hit_rate = precision where labels = (forward_returns > 0), measuring only next-bar direction; actual trade win rate depends on full trade lifecycle (entry through exit), not 1-bar return, creating systematic overestimation of signal quality

quantflow/strategy/research/backtest.py:60-63 -- BacktestEngine is explicitly long-only; ret = (exit_price - entry_price) / entry_price always assumes long direction; short entries from mean_reversion and volatility_breakout are simulated as longs producing guaranteed wrong-direction returns

quantflow/strategy/templates/trend_following.py:168-170 -- exit conditions require vol_ok (volume above threshold) just like entries; requiring volume confirmation to EXIT delays exits during low-volume reversals exactly when you need to exit fastest

candidate_solution.summary: 4 NEW bottlenecks beyond iter1 findings + 3 deeper calibration gaps: (1) RSI-adaptive uses global mean not per-entry, (2) backtest timing mismatch in exit execution, (3) signal_quality hit_rate uses 1-bar proxy not trade lifecycle, (4) vol_ok included in exit conditions delays critical exits; calibration: volume_threshold 0.8 trivial, trailing ATR multipliers too wide, min_conditions too coarse

new_bottlenecks.title: RSI-adaptive profit targets use global mean over ALL entries instead of per-entry RSI -- adaptation is dead code
new_bottlenecks.detail: Lines 260-266: rsi_at_entry = rsi[entries]; avg_entry_rsi = float(rsi_at_entry.mean()). This computes a SINGLE average RSI across ALL historical entries and applies one effective_pct to ALL trades. With 100+ entries over a backtest, the average converges to ~50 (neutral), making the 0.8x/1.2x adjustment trigger only when the entire entry set is collectively overbought/oversold. Individual entries at RSI 80 get the same target as entries at RSI 30 if the global average is 50. This completely defeats the purpose of RSI-adaptive targets. The fix should compute effective_pct per-entry inside the profit_target_exit loop, not globally.
new_bottlenecks.fix: Move RSI-adaptive logic inside profit_target_exit: pass rsi series, compute effective_pct = profit_take_pct * (0.8 if rsi_at_entry > 70 else 1.2 if rsi_at_entry < 30 else 1.0) per individual entry
new_bottlenecks.impact_on_win_rate: -3 to -5%: entries at RSI>70 should have tighter targets (early profit capture) but get average target; entries at RSI<30 should let profits run but get average target cutting winners short

new_bottlenecks.title: BacktestEngine exit timing mismatch -- signals at bar N close execute at bar N+1 open, systematically reducing realized win rate
new_bottlenecks.detail: The backtest loop at lines 112-121: signals from prev_idx (i-1) trigger trades at bar i. But profit_target_exit and trailing_stop compare close-to-close within the signal generation function. When a trailing stop fires at bar N (close < highest - ATR*mult), the backtest actually exits at bar N+1 open. In volatile markets, bar N+1 open can gap significantly from bar N close, causing: (a) winning trades that would have profit-targeted at bar N close to instead exit at a worse price at bar N+1 open, and (b) losing trades to accumulate an extra bar of loss. The 1-bar execution lag systematically reduces backtest win rate vs signal win rate.
new_bottlenecks.fix: BacktestEngine should use close prices for signal execution (same-bar) or explicitly model slippage for next-bar-open execution; profit_target_exit should mark exit bar as the signal bar, not the execution bar
new_bottlenecks.impact_on_win_rate: -2 to -4%: every trailing stop and profit target exit is delayed by 1 bar, during which the trade can reverse against the position

new_bottlenecks.title: signal_quality_metrics hit_rate uses next-bar return as win proxy, not full trade lifecycle -- validation overestimates win rate
new_bottlenecks.detail: Lines 26-28: forward_returns = close.pct_change().shift(-1); labels = (forward_returns > 0).astype(int). This measures whether the NEXT bar's close is higher than current close -- a 1-bar directional proxy. But actual trade win rate depends on the FULL trade lifecycle: entry -> hold -> exit (profit target, trailing stop, max_holding, or signal exit). A signal that correctly predicts next-bar direction (label=1) can still produce a losing trade if the trade is held for max_holding_bars and adverse moves accumulate. Conversely, a signal with wrong next-bar direction can produce a winning trade if the position reverses during the holding period. The CPCV/WFO validation pipeline uses this hit_rate as a GO/NO-GO gate, meaning strategies can pass validation with inflated quality scores.
new_bottlenecks.fix: Add trade-lifecycle win rate to signal_quality_metrics: simulate full entry->exit trades from (entries, exits) signals and compute actual trade win rate; use this alongside 1-bar precision as complementary metrics
new_bottlenecks.impact_on_win_rate: Indirect: validation passes strategies with inflated hit_rate, so deployed strategies have lower actual win rate than validated estimates; estimated gap of 5-10% between validated and realized win rate

new_bottlenecks.title: Exit conditions require volume confirmation (vol_ok), delaying exits during low-volume reversals
new_bottlenecks.detail: Line 168-170: exit_ = int(trend_down) + int(rsi > self._rsi_oversold) + int(vol_ok) + int(atr_ok) >= self._min_conditions. The exit condition set includes vol_ok, meaning a position CANNOT exit unless volume is above threshold. This is counterproductive: reversals and trend breakdowns often occur on LOW volume (distribution phase), exactly when you need fastest exit. Requiring volume confirmation to exit creates a systematic delay that lets winning trades reverse and losing trades accumulate more losses. Only trend_following.py on_bar() has this issue; the generate_signals() version at line 254 uses short_count which also includes vol_ok.
new_bottlenecks.fix: Remove vol_ok from exit condition count, or use a separate min_conditions_exit with lower threshold (e.g., 2 instead of 4) that excludes vol_ok
new_bottlenecks.impact_on_win_rate: -2 to -3%: delayed exits cause profitable trades to reverse before exit triggers, and losing trades to deepen

calibration_gaps.rationale: 3.0 ATR trailing on 1d BTC/USDT (ATR ~$1500-2500) allows $4500-7500 drawdown from peak before exit. Most profitable trend trades close within 2 ATR of peak. 3.0 gives too much room for profits to evaporate. The YAML config sets trailing_stop_atr_multiplier: 1.5 but code reads trailing_stop_atr_mult with default 3.0 -- another key name mismatch.

4h volatility breakouts are fast-moving events. 2.5 ATR trailing gives too much room for the move to reverse. YAML sets trailing_stop_atr_multiplier: 2.0 but code reads trailing_stop_atr_mult with default 2.5 -- key name mismatch makes YAML value dead letter.

Code default 0.8 means vol_ok when volume > 80% of MA -- nearly always true (volume exceeds 80% of its own average ~80% of the time). YAML sets 1.2 which is a meaningful filter. The code default dominates since YAML key mismatch (volume_threshold exists in both but YAML is nested under params.volume_threshold vs code reading volume_threshold from flat params dict).

10 bars at 4h = 40 hours. Bollinger Band lower-band entries on 4h often need 3-5 days (18-30 bars) for price to revert to the opposite band. 10 bars forces exit before reversion completes, turning would-be winners into max_holding losses.

2.0x ATR cap filter rejects entries when volatility > 2x average. But trending moves ARE volatile -- the best trends occur during volatility expansion. 2.0x cap filters out the strongest trend entries. Lowering to 1.5 allows entries during the volatility expansion that accompanies trends.

interaction_effects.issue: The RSI-adaptive global mean bug (NB1) makes adaptive targets dead code. Combined with the LONG-only profit target bug from iter1, SHORT entries from mean_reversion get: (1) wrong direction target check (never fires), and (2) even if direction was fixed, they'd get the global average RSI-based target which is ~50, applying no adaptation. Two bugs compound to make SHORT-side exit completely broken.

Trailing stop fires at bar N close but executes at bar N+1 open in backtest. During strong trends, bar N+1 often opens significantly below bar N close (gap down), causing the trailing stop exit to capture less profit than intended. This interaction is invisible in signal-level analysis but reduces realized win rate.

CPCV and WFO validation use signal_quality_metrics.hit_rate as a quality gate. But hit_rate measures 1-bar precision, not trade-lifecycle win rate. A strategy with 60% 1-bar hit rate can have 45% trade win rate due to adverse holding period. This means validation passes strategies that will underperform in deployment.

interaction_effects.pair: NB4 (vol_ok in exit) + min_conditions entry filter
interaction_effects.issue: Requiring vol_ok in both entry (4 conditions including vol_ok) AND exit means: entries happen during volume surges, exits require volume surges too. But the best exit opportunities (trend reversals, profit targets) often occur on declining volume. The symmetrical requirement creates a lopsided trade lifecycle: easy to enter, hard to exit.

risk_engine._check_strategy_budget sums ALL positions (not filtered by strategy_id) against each strategy's budget. Combined with hardcoded strength values (always 0.7-0.8), Kelly sizing produces uniformly sized positions regardless of signal quality. The budget check sees total portfolio exposure = budget limit faster than intended, blocking legitimate entries.

notes: Iteration 2 confirms and deepens iteration 1 findings. The RSI-adaptive bug (NB1) is MORE severe than iter1 reported: not only is it global mean, but this global mean approach means the feature is completely dead code -- it never meaningfully adjusts targets for individual trades. The YAML key mismatch for trailing_stop_atr_multiplier vs trailing_stop_atr_mult is a NEW finding not in iter1 -- YAML sets 1.5 for trend_following but code defaults to 3.0, meaning trailing stops are 2x wider than operators configure. The signal_quality_metrics 1-bar proxy (NB3) is a systemic issue affecting the entire validation pipeline: CPCV, WFO, and GO/NO-GO gates all use this inflated metric, creating a systematic overestimation of strategy quality.
